bibl.title: Minimal experimental requirements for definition of extracellular vesicles and their functions: a position statement from the International Society fo

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: extracellular vesicles, and what a study must report before it may attribute a cargo or a function to them rather than to whatever co-isolated with them
span.quote: Importantly, it is currently technically challenging to obtain a totally pure EV fraction free from non-vesicular components for functional studies, and therefore there is a need to establish guidelines for analyses of these vesicles and reporting of scientific studies on EV biology.

span.label: what minimal evidence licenses the claim that the material in the tube is EVs, when no method produces a pure EV fraction
span.quote: Separation of these non-vesicular entities from EV is not fully achieved by common EV isolation protocols, including centrifugation protocols or commercial kits that claim EV or “exosome” isolation/purification.

span.label: a minimal set of biochemical, biophysical and functional standards, published as an ISEV position statement, together with an explicit admission that the field cannot yet name markers that would distinguish its own subtypes
span.quote: Unfortunately, the field of EV research has not matured to the point that we can propose a list of EV-specific “markers” that distinguish subsets of EVs from each other, for example, EVs produced via budding from the cell membrane or produced via endosomal compartments.

span.label: method
span.quote: Therefore, we suggest that investigators report the amount of several proteins (3 or more) in at least a semi-quantitative manner in any EV preparation, including EV isolates from body fluids or obtained from secreting cells in vitro

span.label: secreted membrane-enclosed vesicles that co-isolate with non-vesicular carriers of the same cargo - protein complexes and lipoproteins
span.quote: However, the extracellular milieu is more complex as several body fluids (especially serum/plasma) harbour extracellular RNA (exRNA) in other non-EV carriers, including protein complexes (AGO2) ( 4 ) and lipoproteins

span.label: a position statement by the ISEV Executive Committee, with the field's own term usage measured from a PubMed count by year
span.term: a position statement by the ISEV Executive Committee, with the field's own term usage measured from a PubMed count by year
span.quote: An advanced search was performed in PubMed at the end of December 2013 to find, for each year of publication, all articles using the given term (singular or plural) as text word: exosome(s), microvesicles, oncosome(s), ectosome(s), prostasome(s), matrix/calcifying vesicle(s).

span.label: extracellular RNA travels in NON-VESICULAR carriers too - AGO2 protein complexes, HDL and LDL - so a functional result attributed to EVs may belong to something else in the same preparation
span.quote: However, the extracellular milieu is more complex as several body fluids (especially serum/plasma) harbour extracellular RNA (exRNA) in other non-EV carriers, including protein complexes (AGO2) ( 4 ) and lipoproteins

span.label: polymer precipitation, used by commercial kits, does not isolate EVs exclusively and is LIKELY to co-isolate RNA-protein complexes - the named case of a method whose output does not match its label
span.quote: In particular, polymer-based methods to precipitate EVs (used by some commercial kits) do not exclusively isolate EVs, and are likely to co-isolate other molecules, including RNA–protein complexes.

span.label: THE FIELD'S MOST-USED WORD HAS NO AGREED MEANING, SAID IN THE FOUNDING GUIDELINE: `The term “exosomes” is the most commonly used word to designate ANY TYPE OF EV, and this has become a “BUZZ TERM” for EV-related science. The ACTUAL MEANING of this word, however, is NOT UNIVERSALLY ACCEPTED`. The word is simultaneously the most frequent and the least agreed.
span.quote: The term “exosomes” is the most commonly used word to designate any type of EV ( Fig. 1 ), and this has become a “buzz term” for EV-related science. The actual meaning of this word, however, is not universally accepted

span.label: AND THE REASON NO MARKER CAN SETTLE IT IS STATED AS IMMATURITY, NOT DIFFICULTY: `the field of EV research HAS NOT MATURED TO THE POINT that we can propose a list of EV-specific “markers” that distinguish subsets of EVs from each other`. The categories are in use before anything can tell them apart.
span.quote: Unfortunately, the field of EV research has not matured to the point that we can propose a list of EV-specific “markers” that distinguish subsets of EVs from each other, for example, EVs produced via budding from the cell membrane or produced via endosomal compartments

span.label: THE PROTOCOL CHANGES THE OBJECT, STATED IN 2014: `the composition of recovered EVs VARY VASTLY ACCORDING TO THE PROTOCOLS USED`. doyle2019 demonstrates the same thing five years later as `different isolation methods ... from the same cell type results in different proteomic profiles`.
span.quote: Also, the composition of recovered EVs vary vastly according to the protocols used

span.label: THE FIELD'S MOST-USED WORD HAS NO AGREED MEANING, and its own society says so: `exosomes` is `the most commonly used word to designate any type of EV` and `has become a BUZZ TERM`, whose `actual meaning ... is not universally accepted`
span.quote: The term “exosomes” is the most commonly used word to designate any type of EV ( Fig. 1 ), and this has become a “buzz term” for EV-related science. The actual meaning of this word, however, is not universally accepted

span.label: THE FIELD CANNOT NAME THE MARKERS ITS OWN CATEGORIES WOULD NEED: it `has not matured to the point that we can propose a list of EV-specific markers` distinguishing EVs budded from the membrane from those of endosomal origin
span.quote: Unfortunately, the field of EV research has not matured to the point that we can propose a list of EV-specific “markers” that distinguish subsets of EVs from each other, for example, EVs produced via budding from the cell membrane or produced via endosomal compartments.

span.label: the proteins that were taken for markers are `exosome-ENRICHED` and not `exosome-SPECIFIC` - an enrichment describes a tendency and cannot draw a boundary, which is precisely what the names had been doing with it
span.quote: Although numerous proteomic analyses have highlighted proteins commonly found in exosome preparations, it is becoming clear that these do not represent “exosome-specific” markers but rather “exosome-enriched” proteins, as different subsets of secreted EVs contain many common markers.

span.label: there is no consensus gold-standard isolation method and therefore no optimal one to prescribe - the document declines to name a method rather than naming a weak one
span.quote: Since there is currently no consensus on a “gold-standard” method to isolate and/or purify EVs, it cannot be claimed that there is an “optimal” method that should be uniformly used.

span.label: one of the field's terms could not even be COUNTED: `microparticle` was excluded from the term-usage figure because it is massively used for non-vesicles
span.quote: Use of the term microparticle(s) could not be reliably evaluated, since it is massively used to refer to non-vesicle-related particles.

span.label: THE DOCUMENT CALLS ITSELF AN EDITORIAL: `the minimal requirements presented in THIS EDITORIAL`. It is cited ever after as the first of a numbered guideline series, a status conferred on it later by its successor rather than claimed here.
span.quote: We hope that the minimal requirements presented in this editorial therefore will increase awareness of all researchers for potential confounders in their EV-related results

span.label: investigators are asked to report proteins NOT expected to be enriched in EVs - Table I group 3 - alongside the ones that are, in at least a semi-quantitative manner and for three or more proteins
span.note: eliminates: a preparation characterised only by what it was hoped to contain, which cannot reveal co-isolation of other intracellular origins · outcome: absent-declared-unreported
span.quote: Therefore, we suggest that investigators report the amount of several proteins (3 or more) in at least a semi-quantitative manner in any EV preparation, including EV isolates from body fluids or obtained from secreting cells in vitro

span.label: the EV-containing fluid must be collected gently, limiting cell disruption
span.note: eliminates: intracellular vesicles released by mechanical damage being counted as extracellular ones - the document says the term `EVs` MAY NOT BE APPROPRIATE for material isolated that way · outcome: absent-declared-unreported
span.quote: Mechanical disruption of cells or tissues can result in isolation of vesicles that originate from the intracellular compartments, which obviously would reduce the purity of EVs. Therefore, the term “EVs” may not be appropriate for materials isolated in such ways.

span.label: the field's own term usage is counted from PubMed by year, with non-EV senses of `exosome` and `microvesicle` manually removed
span.note: eliminates: an impression about which words the literature uses, replaced by a count - and the count is honest about what it could NOT measure · outcome: partial
span.quote: An advanced search was performed in PubMed at the end of December 2013 to find, for each year of publication, all articles using the given term (singular or plural) as text word: exosome(s), microvesicles, oncosome(s), ectosome(s), prostasome(s), matrix/calcifying vesicle(s).

span.label: whether any isolation method yields a pure EV fraction, or whether one can be named as the standard
span.note: eliminates: nothing - the document reports that a totally pure fraction is technically challenging to obtain and that there is no consensus gold standard · outcome: failed
span.quote: Importantly, it is currently technically challenging to obtain a totally pure EV fraction free from non-vesicular components for functional studies, and therefore there is a need to establish guidelines for analyses of these vesicles and reporting of scientific studies on EV biology.

span.label: extracellular vesicles
span.quote: Secreted membrane-enclosed vesicles, collectively called extracellular vesicles (EVs), which include exosomes, ectosomes, microvesicles, microparticles, apoptotic bodies and other EV subsets, encompass a very rapidly growing scientific field in biology and medicine.

span.label: exosomes
span.quote: The term “exosomes” is the most commonly used word to designate any type of EV ( Fig. 1 ), and this has become a “buzz term” for EV-related science. The actual meaning of this word, however, is not universally accepted

span.label: microvesicles
span.quote: Secreted membrane-enclosed vesicles, collectively called extracellular vesicles (EVs), which include exosomes, ectosomes, microvesicles, microparticles, apoptotic bodies and other EV subsets, encompass a very rapidly growing scientific field in biology and medicine.

span.label: markers
span.quote: Unfortunately, the field of EV research has not matured to the point that we can propose a list of EV-specific “markers” that distinguish subsets of EVs from each other, for example, EVs produced via budding from the cell membrane or produced via endosomal compartments.

span.label: lipoproteins
span.quote: However, the extracellular milieu is more complex as several body fluids (especially serum/plasma) harbour extracellular RNA (exRNA) in other non-EV carriers, including protein complexes (AGO2) ( 4 ) and lipoproteins

span.label: gold-standard
span.quote: Since there is currently no consensus on a “gold-standard” method to isolate and/or purify EVs, it cannot be claimed that there is an “optimal” method that should be uniformly used

span.label: buzz term
span.quote: The term “exosomes” is the most commonly used word to designate any type of EV ( Fig. 1 ), and this has become a “buzz term” for EV-related science. The actual meaning of this word, however, is not universally accepted

span.label: extracellular vesicles
span.quote: whereas the term “extracellular vesicles,” chosen as generic term at creation of ISEV in September 2011, is steadily growing

span.label: extracellular vesicles, 2014 - AS DEFINED HERE BY ENUMERATION, not by property: `exosomes, ectosomes, microvesicles, microparticles, apoptotic bodies and other EV subsets`. The 2023 statement replaces this with three properties (released, bilayer-delimited, non-replicating); THE LIST CAME FIRST AND THE PROPERTY CAME AFTER
span.quote: Secreted membrane-enclosed vesicles, collectively called extracellular vesicles (EVs), which include exosomes, ectosomes, microvesicles, microparticles, apoptotic bodies and other EV subsets, encompass a very rapidly growing scientific field in biology and medicine.

span.label: exosome, 2014 - A BUZZ TERM BY ITS OWN SOCIETY'S ACCOUNT. Used for any EV in practice, defined by endosomal origin in principle, and the isolated material `generally contains a mixture of EVs`. The 2023 statement discourages the word; this one only records that its meaning is not agreed
span.quote: The term “exosomes” is the most commonly used word to designate any type of EV ( Fig. 1 ), and this has become a “buzz term” for EV-related science. The actual meaning of this word, however, is not universally accepted

span.label: `exosome-enriched` versus `exosome-specific` - THE DISTINCTION THE WHOLE PROBLEM TURNS ON, drawn here in 2014. A marker that is merely enriched cannot separate subsets; the field's subtype names had been treating enrichment as though it were specificity
span.quote: Although numerous proteomic analyses have highlighted proteins commonly found in exosome preparations, it is becoming clear that these do not represent “exosome-specific” markers but rather “exosome-enriched” proteins, as different subsets of secreted EVs contain many common markers.

span.label: the 2014 HOPE - `we hope to eventually be able to provide specific markers and characteristics of EV subtypes`. READ AGAINST MISEV2023, WHICH REPORTS NO UNIVERSAL MARKERS AND DISCOURAGES THE TERMS, this is a field holding a definition open for nine years and then closing it the other way
span.quote: These criteria will be updated with improvements in the “state of the art,” and we hope to eventually be able to provide specific markers and characteristics of EV subtypes.

span.label: `gold-standard` DENIED, WITH THE CONSEQUENCE DRAWN: `Since there is currently NO CONSENSUS on a “gold-standard” method to isolate and/or purify EVs, IT CANNOT BE CLAIMED THAT THERE IS AN “OPTIMAL” METHOD that should be uniformly used.` The absence of agreement is treated as barring a claim, not merely as an open question.
span.quote: Since there is currently no consensus on a “gold-standard” method to isolate and/or purify EVs, it cannot be claimed that there is an “optimal” method that should be uniformly used

span.label: A SOCIETY NAMES A CATEGORY AND THE LITERATURE DOES NOT FOLLOW: `the term “extracellular vesicles,” CHOSEN AS GENERIC TERM AT CREATION OF ISEV in September 2011, is steadily growing` - while `from 2004 onwards, the term “exosome” has become the most often used`. A dated act of naming, and a measured record of it not taking.
span.quote: whereas the term “extracellular vesicles,” chosen as generic term at creation of ISEV in September 2011, is steadily growing

span.label: critiques → commercial EV/exosome isolation kits and polymer precipitation methods, on the ground that they do not isolate EVs exclusively and co-isolate RNA-protein complexes
span.quote: In particular, polymer-based methods to precipitate EVs (used by some commercial kits) do not exclusively isolate EVs, and are likely to co-isolate other molecules, including RNA–protein complexes.

span.label: critiques → the use of `exosome` as a category label, on the ground that its meaning is not universally accepted and the isolated material is a mixture
span.quote: The term “exosomes” is the most commonly used word to designate any type of EV ( Fig. 1 ), and this has become a “buzz term” for EV-related science. The actual meaning of this word, however, is not universally accepted

span.label: critiques → attributing a cargo or function to EVs from a preparation that also contains AGO2 complexes and lipoproteins carrying the same extracellular RNA
span.quote: However, the extracellular milieu is more complex as several body fluids (especially serum/plasma) harbour extracellular RNA (exRNA) in other non-EV carriers, including protein complexes (AGO2) ( 4 ) and lipoproteins

span.quote: Notably, from 2004 onwards, the term “exosome” has become the most often used in published articles describing EVs, whereas the term “extracellular vesicles,” chosen as generic term at creation of ISEV in September 2011, is steadily growing.

span.quote: Secreted membrane-enclosed vesicles, collectively called extracellular vesicles (EVs), which include exosomes, ectosomes, microvesicles, microparticles, apoptotic bodies and other EV subsets, encompass a very rapidly growing scientific field in biology and medicine.
